events.title: The death of Adrian IV, the only English pope
events.shortBlurb: Nicholas Breakspear of Hertfordshire, the only Englishman ever to sit in Peter's chair, died at Anagni, and a disputed succession opened a long schism…
body: Nicholas Breakspear, born about 1100 at Abbots Langley near St. Albans in Hertfordshire, rose from the cloister of St. Rufus to be cardinal-bishop of Albano and the legate who ordered the Church in Scandinavia, erecting Nidaros as its archbishopric. On 4 December 1154 the cardinals chose him pope as Adrian IV, and no other Englishman has sat in Peter's chair since.

His five years were stormy. He crowned Frederick Barbarossa emperor in 1155, quarreled with him two years later at Besançon over the word 'benefice,' made peace with the Norman king of Sicily at Benevento, and, by the bull Laudabiliter — a document whose authenticity scholars still dispute — is said to have granted Henry II of England the lordship of Ireland. Rome itself, in the grip of the commune and of Arnold of Brescia, he could hardly hold, and he spent much of his pontificate away from it.

On 1 September 1159, at Anagni, he died suddenly; the chroniclers tell a strange tale of a fly caught in his throat, while later writers suppose a quinsy. Within days the double election of Alexander III and the antipope Victor IV split the Church in a schism of eighteen years, and Adrian was laid in St. Peter's, the one English pope.
